vivaQuestions.question: How does your model work?
vivaQuestions.answer: Ridge combines the features using learned weights. Its alpha penalty discourages very large weights, which can stabilize predictions when engine size and power are correlated.

vivaQuestions.question: Which parameters did you change?
vivaQuestions.answer: alpha controls the penalty on large coefficients. Compare the default alpha of 1 with 10.

vivaQuestions.question: What are this model’s limitations?
vivaQuestions.answer: A straight-line relationship may miss interactions and nonlinear depreciation. Coefficient size depends on feature scaling, so it is not a universal feature-importance ranking.

vivaQuestions.question: What are the training, validation and test sets for?
vivaQuestions.answer: Development training teaches the four variants. Validation compares them and selects the settings and target transformation. The selected version is retrained on the full Assignment 1 training set and evaluated once on its labelled holdout. All members use the same files.

vivaQuestions.question: Why are there two extra tuning files?
vivaQuestions.answer: Splitting already-imputed and scaled data would let validation rows influence training medians and scaling. The extra files were split from raw outer-training rows first and processed using development-training statistics only. The shared preparation notebook shows every step. Assignment 1 is not replaced.

vivaQuestions.question: Why compare Price and Log_Price?
vivaQuestions.answer: This is the preprocessing variation: the target is used either directly or as log1p(Price). Logs compress large prices. np.expm1 reverses the transformation before computing errors. Both versions are scored in price units.

vivaQuestions.question: What does manual tuning mean here?
vivaQuestions.answer: We compare two explicit parameter settings, each with two target choices. That gives four variants of one algorithm. The lowest validation RMSE wins. This is a small manual search, not an exhaustive search and not cross-validation.

vivaQuestions.question: Why use RMSE, MAE and R²?
vivaQuestions.answer: RMSE is the main metric because larger price errors receive a larger penalty. MAE is average absolute error. Both use INR lakhs. R² compares squared error with predicting the evaluation-set mean. It can be negative and is not percentage accuracy.

vivaQuestions.question: How does the group compare its six algorithms?
vivaQuestions.answer: Compare the chosen variants on the same validation set, using validation RMSE to select the group model and its holdout scores to assess generalization. You can also report the observed holdout ranking, but choosing from it makes it part of model selection.

vivaQuestions.question: What are the limitations?
vivaQuestions.answer: One validation split is less stable than repeated cross-validation, and four variants cover only a small set of possibilities. Scores describe the kilometre-filtered population. The original mileage-unit and zero-value limitations remain, and earlier EDA saw the full dataset. These historical Indian prices do not establish current Sri Lankan prices.

vivaQuestions.question: Can we evaluate university test predictions?
vivaQuestions.answer: The university test file has no Price labels. We preserve all 1,234 rows and produce predictions, but cannot calculate its RMSE, MAE or R².

vivaQuestions.question: How does your model work?
vivaQuestions.answer: KNN stores the training cars. At prediction time it finds nearby cars in feature space and averages their targets. Distance weighting gives nearer cars more influence.

vivaQuestions.question: Which parameters did you change?
vivaQuestions.answer: Compare the default 5 equally weighted neighbours with 9 neighbours weighted by distance. Nearby cars then have more influence.

vivaQuestions.question: What are this model’s limitations?
vivaQuestions.answer: Small K can follow noise; large K can smooth away useful local differences. Distances depend on scaling and feature choice. We retain Assignment 1’s five scaled columns, with seats and ownership in their original units.

vivaQuestions.question: What are the training, validation and test sets for?
vivaQuestions.answer: Development training teaches the four variants. Validation compares them and selects the settings and target transformation. The selected version is retrained on the full Assignment 1 training set and evaluated once on its labelled holdout. All members use the same files.

vivaQuestions.question: Why are there two extra tuning files?
vivaQuestions.answer: Splitting already-imputed and scaled data would let validation rows influence training medians and scaling. The extra files were split from raw outer-training rows first and processed using development-training statistics only. The shared preparation notebook shows every step. Assignment 1 is not replaced.

vivaQuestions.question: Why compare Price and Log_Price?
vivaQuestions.answer: This is the preprocessing variation: the target is used either directly or as log1p(Price). Logs compress large prices. np.expm1 reverses the transformation before computing errors. Both versions are scored in price units.

vivaQuestions.question: What does manual tuning mean here?
vivaQuestions.answer: We compare two explicit parameter settings, each with two target choices. That gives four variants of one algorithm. The lowest validation RMSE wins. This is a small manual search, not an exhaustive search and not cross-validation.

vivaQuestions.question: Why use RMSE, MAE and R²?
vivaQuestions.answer: RMSE is the main metric because larger price errors receive a larger penalty. MAE is average absolute error. Both use INR lakhs. R² compares squared error with predicting the evaluation-set mean. It can be negative and is not percentage accuracy.

vivaQuestions.question: How does the group compare its six algorithms?
vivaQuestions.answer: Compare the chosen variants on the same validation set, using validation RMSE to select the group model and its holdout scores to assess generalization. You can also report the observed holdout ranking, but choosing from it makes it part of model selection.

vivaQuestions.question: What are the limitations?
vivaQuestions.answer: One validation split is less stable than repeated cross-validation, and four variants cover only a small set of possibilities. Scores describe the kilometre-filtered population. The original mileage-unit and zero-value limitations remain, and earlier EDA saw the full dataset. These historical Indian prices do not establish current Sri Lankan prices.

vivaQuestions.question: Can we evaluate university test predictions?
vivaQuestions.answer: The university test file has no Price labels. We preserve all 1,234 rows and produce predictions, but cannot calculate its RMSE, MAE or R².
